title: Ridge reference with the scaling of N2_total_mvc
hypothesis: Deterministic per-position ridge regression on the same inputs: a simple reference the LSTM should beat.
motivation: Fixed settings for the whole normalization study: total torque (no passive subtraction), balanced positions (each position's target divided by its standard deviation), clean passive table not used (nothing is subtracted), 0.2 s window, no auto-gain, LSTM 8x2, original training settings, learn session 1 -> predict session 2.

dashboard.label: Ridge reference · MVC peak
dashboard.name: Ridge regression reference · EMG ÷ MVC peak

text.purpose: Reference model, never chosen: per-position ridge regression with the scaling of N2. Each muscle is divided by its peak during the maximum-effort trials, recorded once at the start of the visit. The EMG becomes a percentage of maximal activation. Session 2 is divided by the same numbers.
text.target: Total measured torque, nothing subtracted. The passive table plays no part in training or scoring.
text.protocol: Train on session 1, test on session 2. Total torque, 0.2 s window (20 samples at 100 Hz) of four muscle envelopes plus angle. Ridge regression with its own coefficients per position, no seeds. People: CH, EG, HM, IES, JM, YES. Seeds: 0.

settings: Session 1 → session 2 · 8 angles · one ~90 s trial per angle
4 EMG envelopes (GM, GL, SOL, TA) + ankle angle, 100 Hz
0.2 s = 20 samples → torque at the window’s last sample
steps: EMG: band-pass 30–300 Hz, rectify, 2 Hz low-pass → envelope (1 kHz), then down-sampled to 100 Hz.
Scale: Each muscle envelope is divided by its peak during the maximum-effort trials. Session 2 is divided by the same four numbers.
Standardise the 5 inputs (mean 0, sd 1) with session 1’s training statistics.
Cut 0.2 s windows sliding by one sample. Each session-1 trial: first 80 % to fit, last 20 % to stop training.
Fit one ridge regression per position on EMG, EMG² and angle features; predict session 2.
Score each position on every 100 Hz sample: R² = 1 − Σ(y − ŷ)² / Σ(y − ȳ)², MAE = mean |y − ŷ|. Median over seeds, then median across positions; R² below 0 is shown as 0.
